title: I Used the Kintsugi Gold-Dust Log on the Mentor Who Palmed My Vial

parts.text: I opened kit five at 3:06 p.m. and mentor Aya was already dusting from my numbered vial. The card said: ONE KIT. TWO HOURS. DUST STAYS WITH THE LOG. I was thirty-nine, studio member, holding a bowl that listed our join. Aya shrugged. "Mentors are the gold." I photographed the card, the log, and her brush on my vial. Then I asked for the dust sheet. At 3:14 the studio pinged why Aya's name was on my gold. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Aya's brush on my vial during our kit.

social.video_title: She dusted from my numbered vial on my join — Part 1/2
social.description: Kintsugi kit, a mentor on my vial, a two-hour log she posted. I logged the brush. Would you have asked for the dust sheet?

parts.text: Aya called it a test until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the brush still. The vial went back to my kit. Aya ran her own two hours and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about join. Join is a word mentors use when a log exists. Kit policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE GOLD. I keep our vial on a labeled tray. Aya brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Dust sheet, numbered vial, and a second line on the card. Was a test ever my join?
